instruction: Change the slide size to 20 cm wide and 25 cm tall in the Slide Properties.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to change slide orientation from landscape to portrait. First tried the Properties panel dropdown, then navigated to Slide > Slide Properties dialog. Successfully selected Portrait radio button and clicked OK. Slide visually changed to portrait but evaluator returned score 0.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Impress menus, open Slide Properties dialog, change radio buttons and settings in dialogs, interact with Properties panel
metadata.failure_analysis: Model correctly performed the orientation change visually, but check_slide_orientation_Portrait returned 0. Possible issue with file save timing or format compatibility.
metadata.task_rationale: The model demonstrated it can navigate to Slide Properties and modify dimension-related settings. This task tests the same dialog interaction but requires entering specific numeric values for width and height.
metadata.explanation: Task requires opening Slide > Slide Properties and setting custom width (20 cm) and height (25 cm). Custom getter reads slide dimensions from the saved pptx using python-pptx. Custom metric checks dimensions with 0.5 cm tolerance and awards partial credit (0.5 per correct dimension).

scoring_breakdown.width: 0.5 - Slide width matches 20 cm within tolerance
scoring_breakdown.height: 0.5 - Slide height matches 25 cm within tolerance

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts slide width and height in cm from pptx file using python-pptx's slide_width.cm and slide_height.cm properties

Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses expected.get('expected_width_cm'), expected.get('expected_height_cm'), expected.get('tolerance_cm') without incorrect nesting
Complete coverage: both width (20 cm) and height (25 cm) requirements from the instruction are verified with appropriate partial credit (0.5 each)
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring dimensions reflect the user's changes
Expected values (20.0 cm width, 25.0 cm height) exactly match the instruction requirements
Tolerance of 0.5 cm is reasonable for unit conversion rounding in LibreOffice
Data flow is correct: getter returns {width_cm, height_cm} dict, metric reads result.get('width_cm') and result.get('height_cm') — fully compatible
